rule: Written before the report period (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-23) was run for the first time. That period is run once, with this code and every experiment in run.ts unchanged. Nothing is retuned after seeing it.

chosenConfiguration.what: The gap rules only (buy when HSKSwap trades below the exchange consensus by more than the round-trip cost), through the gate, with rule-based sizing. Trend rules switched off. Thresholds, vault policy and owner limits unchanged from the defaults written on 2026-11-24 before any history was downloaded.
why: On development, trend buys lost money at every horizon measured: the 121 episodes the gate refused for cost returned -59 bps on average after 24 hours, and -58 bps after subtracting the exchange's own move.
The trend exit closed gap positions before the gap had closed: 9 such exits averaged -44 bps, against +220 bps for the 7 positions that reached their target.
Gap buys the gate passed beat the exchange's own move by 94 bps on average after 24 hours (40 episodes); those it refused for too small an edge beat it by 24 bps (29 episodes).

changesMadeDuringDevelopment: Positions are now built only up to half of what one sale can take out of the pool inside the vault's slippage limit, and a sale that does not fit is split. Before this, a position at the vault's 30% cap could not be sold in the shallow pool and sat for days; its result was luck.
The simulator carries our own price impact forward until the next recorded swap. Before this, several buys in a quiet pool were each priced as if the others had not happened.
The simulator assumes the pool's oracle had been enlarged before the vault listed it. As recorded (one slot until 2026-10-26) every vault buy would have reverted.
knownBeforehandAboutTheReportPeriod: The whole history was inspected for data quality before any strategy result existed. That showed the pool's liquidity was withdrawn on 2026-10-10 07:57 UTC and returned on 2026-10-16 03:48 UTC, and that the oracle was enlarged on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-31. No price or signal statistics of the report period were looked at.
expectations: `trend-only` ends near zero and `aggressive` ends below `sizing`.
While the pool is empty (2026-10-10 to 2026-10-16) no trade executes; a position held going in stays open and cannot be stopped out.
Returns are within a few percent of zero either way and each configuration closes at most a few dozen positions, so no claim of statistical significance will be made in either direction.
